text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The government has stopped work on all new development schemes, official sources said.
- A decision on revamping and depoliticising the police department is expected to be taken by the government on Wednesday, sources said.
- The railways general manager suspended the services of 11 employees for negligence of duty that caused the train crash last Monday near the town of Khanewal in Punjab province.

- The economic coordination committee which met under the chairmanship of Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz was informed that 0.9 million tonnes of wheat is being imported from the U.S. to meet domestic demand for the next three months.
- Another earthquake of moderate intensity rocked Quetta and Sibi but caused no damage or casualties.

- The International Narcotics Control Board has asked Pakistan to give "highest priority" to the implementation of the federal narcotics legislation in the tribal areas, a major centre of drug production and trafficking.
- The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry has asked the government to hand over the mining of precious and semi-precious stones to the private sector.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz has stressed the need to bring down the deficit in the current account.
- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub is expected to meet his Indian counter-part I.K. Gujral in New Dehli next month during the Non- Aligned Movement foreign ministers' conference.
- Pakistan's private Highnoon Group of Industries will export $200 million worth medicines to Iraq.
- The state-run Pakistan National Shipping Coporation plans to purchase two bulk carriers of 35,000 tonnes DWT.
- The Indian Sugar & General Industry Export Import Corporation Ltd has indicated that it will be able to supply 45,220 tonnes of sugar to two Pakistani firms.
- Ginners have asked the government to provide $25 million subsidy to export raw cotton worth $575 million lying in stock with them.
THE NEWS
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has abolished discretionary quotas at federal and provincial levels and ordered distribution of state land among landless farmers.

- The government will observe simplicity and austerity during the forthcoming OIC Summit conference and heads of states and othr dignitaries will be taken to the venue of the summit in passenger vans instead of luxury cars.
